response.justification: The candidate is a versatile, experienced full-stack engineer with nearly two decades of software development across web, mobile, and some systems programming, but he falls well short of the core minimum qualifications: he has only brief professional C++ exposure (a ~6-month stint at National Instruments plus a thesis project) versus the required 8 years, and his infrastructure/distributed-systems experience is limited to roughly two years of low-latency DLang work rather than sustained large-scale compute platform engineering. He also lacks demonstrated technical leadership of cloud/DevOps teams, making him a poor fit for this specific C++-centric platform lead role despite strong general engineering credentials.
strengths: Broad, long-tenured engineering career with strong testing culture (TDD, CI/CD, trunk-based development)
Real low-latency, high-throughput systems experience (millions of HTTP requests/sec at Sociomantic using async I/O, fibers, caching)
Proven mentorship and knowledge-sharing track record (workshops, courses, coding dojos, open-source maintainership)
concerns: Far below the required 8 years of C++ experience; recent work is TypeScript/Node.js-focused
Limited large-scale cloud compute/infrastructure platform experience; most roles are product/web engineering
No formal technical leadership role managing priorities, deadlines, or mentoring cloud/DevOps engineers

key_factors.factor: Limited cloud infrastructure and technical leadership background
Strong general engineering depth and mentoring aptitude
